claims.validation_command: cargo build --release -p velesdb-server && stat -c%s target/release/velesdb-server  # measured 2026-09-02 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: 14345984 bytes = 13.68 MiB
claims.source: Measured 2026-09-02 from `cargo build --release -p velesdb-server` on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: 14345984 bytes (13.68 MiB); [profile.release] already sets strip = true. The Binary Size Gate measured 13.78 MiB for the same commit on ubuntu-latest with toolchain 1.90, a 10 KB delta. The figure this replaces (~10 MB) was measured at 4.0.0 on aarch64-apple-darwin and was never true for the Linux x86_64 build users download: v5.2.0, already published, builds to 14339664 bytes (13.68 MiB) on the same machine, so 6.0.0 adds 6320 bytes (0.04%) rather than regressing. Two things kept that invisible. binary-size.yml piped the gate's exit status into tee under a shell without pipefail, so the required check could not fail on an over-ceiling binary (#2193). And this entry's previous source cited a "README footnote [3]" stating a 7-13 MB provenance range - that footnote does not exist; README.md carries no footnotes at all, so readers saw a flat ~10 MB with no range. Apple Silicon is smaller and has not been re-measured since 4.0.0; ~14 MB is quoted for the largest target rather than the smallest.

claims.validation_command: cd crates/velesdb-wasm && wasm-pack build --target web --release && gzip -c pkg/velesdb_wasm_bg.wasm | wc -c  # measured 2026-09-02: 726700 bytes = 710 KiB (raw 2114045 = 2.02 MiB)
claims.source: Measured 2026-09-02 at 6.0.0 with `wasm-pack build --target web --release`, the command release.yml:623 publishes from: pkg/velesdb_wasm_bg.wasm is 2114045 bytes raw and 726700 gzipped (level 6) = 710 KiB. The ~674 KB it replaces was measured on the published 4.0.0 npm package and had drifted 5.4% low over two majors. This entry's previous waiver said the figure could only come from the published npm artifact of the next release, and that "the WASM Build Check job bounds regressions meanwhile" - that job runs cargo check, quantization-parity tests and wasm-bindgen tests and never measures bundle size, so nothing bounded anything. The validation_command above removes the chicken-and-egg by measuring the same artifact from source, before the tag rather than after it. Caveat on the last percent: the measurement used wasm-pack 0.13.1 with binaryen 117, while CI installs the latest wasm-pack via taiki-e/install-action, which may pin a different binaryen; wasm-opt settings come from [package.metadata.wasm-pack.profile.release] (-Os, SIMD, bulk-memory, nontrapping-float-to-int) either way. wasm-opt MUST run for this number to mean anything - skipping it yields 703535 gzipped from a larger 2294177-byte raw bundle, which is not the published artifact.
